methods.name: EF v3.1
methods.description: Environmental Footprint 3.1 (EU JRC): the 25 EF indicators MApper's indicator mapping, AESA and Impact Assessment use
methods.long_description: Installs the 25 EF v3.1 methods (11,414 characterisation factors on 3,226 flows) from the factors that ship with the installed Brightway software (the ecoinvent 3.9 LCIA implementation), so it works offline. Only EF v3.1 is installed, not the other ~760 methods. The factors are linked to this project's existing biosphere3, which is only read: no flow is added, changed or removed. Factors on flows the biosphere3 does not contain are skipped, counted and listed after the install; against an ecoinvent 3.10 or 3.11 biosphere3 about 9% of the factors are skipped. What the skipped metal factors mean, measured on ecoinvent 3.10 projects: most of them sit on old ore-style flows (for example "Copper, 0.52% in sulfide…") that no ecoinvent 3.10 or 3.11 exchange uses, so they cost nothing. The real gap is flows that the bundled ecoinvent 3.9 data does not characterise at all: the rare earths, hafnium and scandium, and rhodium, ruthenium, osmium and iridium among the platinum-group metals; graphite is uncharacterised too. The flows named here are about 26% of the exchanges on metal flows in the audited projects (graphite not counted), but about 0.005% of the metal mass of one NMC811 battery (measured with the EF factors). A project can hold several ecoinvent versions only if its biosphere3 contains the flows of all of them.
methods.citation: Andreasi Bassi, S., et al. (2023). Updated characterisation and normalisation factors for the Environmental Footprint 3.1 method. EUR 31414 EN, Publications Office of the European Union.
methods.notes: Offline. Needs an ecoinvent database (and so its biosphere3) already imported into the project.

methods.name: ReCiPe 2016 midpoint (H, I, E)
methods.description: ReCiPe 2016 v1.03 midpoint, hierarchist, individualist and egalitarian perspectives
methods.long_description: Installs 54 methods (22,986 characterisation factors). All three perspectives are installed together (18 midpoint indicators each, long-term emissions included); they share the same flows and differ only in time horizon and assumptions, so pick one in the impact assessment. The 'no long-term' variants are not part of this entry. Installs from the factors that ship with the installed Brightway software (the ecoinvent 3.9 LCIA implementation), so it works offline and downloads nothing. The factors are linked to this project's existing biosphere3 by flow code, then by name and compartment; biosphere3 is only read, no flow is added, changed or removed, and a method already in the project is never overwritten. Factors on flows the project's biosphere3 does not hold are skipped, counted and listed after the install. What the skipped metal factors mean, measured on ecoinvent 3.10 projects: most of them sit on old ore-style flows (for example "Copper, 0.52% in sulfide…") that no ecoinvent 3.10 or 3.11 exchange uses, so they cost nothing. The real gap is flows that the bundled ecoinvent 3.9 data does not characterise at all: the rare earths, hafnium and scandium, and rhodium, ruthenium, osmium and iridium among the platinum-group metals; graphite is uncharacterised too. The flows named here are about 26% of the exchanges on metal flows in the audited projects (graphite not counted), but about 0.005% of the metal mass of one NMC811 battery (measured with the EF factors). A project can hold several ecoinvent versions only if its biosphere3 contains the flows of all of them.
methods.citation: Huijbregts, M.A.J., et al. (2017). ReCiPe2016: a harmonised life cycle impact assessment method at midpoint and endpoint level. Int J Life Cycle Assess 22, 138-147.
methods.notes: Offline. Needs an ecoinvent database (and so its biosphere3) already imported into the project.

methods.name: IMPACT World+ 2.2.1
methods.long_description: Midpoint, expert and footprint versions. Covers ~18 midpoint categories with regionalized characterisation factors. CIRAIG.
methods.citation: Bulle, C., et al. (2019). IMPACT World+: a globally regionalized life cycle impact assessment method. Int J Life Cycle Assess 24, 1653-1674.
methods.factor_source: The characterisation factors come from the IMPACT World+ 2.2.1 Brightway package published on Zenodo, downloaded when you install (the variant built for your project's ecoinvent version); the package links them to biosphere3 itself, so this app shows no linked or skipped count for it.

methods.name: LC-IMPACT
methods.description: GLAM-aligned damage method, Verones et al. (2020)
methods.long_description: Global non-regionalized variant of LC-IMPACT. 22 methods across climate, land use, particulate matter, and water. Installed via the bw2_lcimpact package by Chris Mutel.
methods.citation: Verones, F., et al. (2020). LC-IMPACT: A regionalized life cycle damage assessment method. Journal of Industrial Ecology 24(6), 1201-1219.
methods.notes: Requires internet + pip at install time. First install downloads the Python package (~1 MB). Last released 2022-04, so biosphere flow remapping may be required for newer biosphere3 versions.
methods.factor_source: The characterisation factors come from the bw2_lcimpact Python package (version 0.4.2), which pip downloads when you install; the package links them to biosphere3 itself, so this app shows no linked or skipped count for it.
